newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish stocks flat in thin trade ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Irish stocks flat in thin trade ahead of weekend.

text.p: The Irish bourse tugged at anchor amid minimal levels of trade on Friday, with little news to motivate the market either way, dealers said.
"It's the end of a fairly intense week, and everything is winding down," a dealer said.
"With little in the way of features, either international or domestic, investors are taking a breather."
By 1530 GMT, the ISEQ index of shares was up 10.31 points, or 0.28 percent at 3642.01.
Elsewhere, London's main FTSE index bounced from the day's lows but remained weak, tracking the Dow.
Markets were largely unruffled by stronger than expected U.S. durable goods orders.
Among leading financials, Allied Irish Banks Plc was unchanged at 598p, while Bank of Ireland shed 2.0 pence to 837.
Elsewhere in the financial sector, Irish Life Plc fell 5-3/4 pence to 365.25, and Irish Permanent Plc firmed 3.0 pence to 668.
Among leading industrials, CRH Plc slipped 3.0 pence to 685, while Jefferson Smurfit Group Plc was off 2.5 pence to 213. Both stocks were lower on profit-taking, dealers said.
Meanwhile, Waterford Foods Plc gained 7.0 pence to 177 and Avonmore Foods Plc rose 3.0 pence to 310 after shareholders of both companies approved their merger plan.

Jurys Hotel Group Plc firmed 5.0 pence to 415, Greencore Group Plc shed 7.0 pence to 325 and Hibernian Group Plc rose 10 pence to 400 ahead of results due next week. --Kevin Smith, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 676 9779
